rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient at moderate temperature to elute all 8 compounds if possible and map the overall elution window without risking truncation. This should reveal whether peaks are compressed early or late and guide narrowing the phi window and adjusting slope in the next runs.

All peaks eluted between about 4.1 and 9.4 min, corresponding to roughly phi_e 0.20 to 0.44, so narrowing the gradient window around the observed elution window should improve selectivity and keep all peaks inside the gradient. Keeping tG and T fixed isolates the effect of the phi window on the unresolved 4/5 pair.

The narrowed window fully resolved all pairs, so now the limiting factor is time; shorten tG to pull the last peak back toward 10 min while staying in the same selective window. This tests how much resolution margin the method has before any pair drops below 1.5.

At tG 12 the slope became too steep and two pairs collapsed, while tG 20 had ample resolution but excessive retention, so tG 16 is the logical midpoint to recover both critical pairs while trimming time. Holding the same phi window and temperature isolates the slope effect and may land near the best tradeoff.

The current method is fully resolved but slightly too slow, so a modest increase in phi1 should bring the late peaks earlier with limited impact on the already adequate critical resolutions. Keeping phi0 and tG fixed targets time reduction while preserving the selective region around the troublesome middle pair.

The 0.20–0.45, 16 min method is fully resolved but a bit late; raising temperature should shorten retention and may preserve or even improve the close-pair selectivity better than increasing phi1 did. This directly tests whether temperature can move t_last toward 10 min without collapsing the 4/5 and 6/7 pairs.

At 45 C the method is close to the current optimum, with only one mildly subcritical pair and a modest time penalty; shortening tG slightly may bring t_last nearer 10 min while potentially keeping that pair near acceptable resolution. This probes whether the best tradeoff lies just steeper than the current 16 min, 45 C condition.

The only remaining weak point is the early-middle 3/4 pair, suggesting the lower end of the window is too high; dropping phi0 by one step should give that region more gradient space and may improve their selectivity without much effect on the last peak. Keeping phi1, tG, and T fixed cleanly tests whether the critical pair responds to the low-phi boundary rather than slope or temperature.

Lowering phi0 hurt both time and the critical 3/4 pair, so instead tighten the upper end of the window to focus gradient volume on the observed elution region and potentially improve selectivity around 3/4 while keeping the run short. This tests whether the problematic pair responds to a narrower overall window rather than a lower starting composition.

The 3/4 pair is nearly insensitive to phi-window changes but changed identity with temperature, so another 5 C increase is the best lever to try for a favorable selectivity shift while also reducing the small time penalty. This may move the last peak to about 10 min and potentially lift the only subcritical pair over 1.5.

Temperature at 50 C collapsed the critical 3/4 pair, so stay at 45 C and instead shorten tG one step from the current best condition to reduce the small remaining time penalty. This will show whether CRF can be improved further by trading a little resolution margin elsewhere while keeping the temperature-driven selectivity that avoids catastrophic coelution.

The current best already has no time penalty, so the only possible gain is if a slightly steeper method still keeps the near-critical pairs acceptable while shortening further. Testing tG 10 maps the cliff edge below the optimum and tells us whether injection 11 is truly near-maximal or if more speed is available.

tG 12 at 45 C is the best region so far, and the limiting issue is two slightly subcritical pairs; increasing phi1 at the same slope conditions may shift selectivity enough to improve the 3/4 pair while keeping t_last under 10 min. This tests whether a modestly wider upper window can outperform the current best without reintroducing a time penalty.

Changing phi1 upward had no effect because the late peaks already elute before reaching that part of the gradient, so the useful remaining handle is phi0. Raising phi0 one step may selectively alter the early-middle region containing the 3/4 pair while maintaining the fast, zero-penalty run time of the current best.

The two near-critical pairs respond strongly to temperature, and 45 C gave the best overall balance but still left 3/4 and 6/7 just below full credit; dropping to 35 C from the same fast method is the best remaining way to seek a different selectivity pattern. This directly tests whether a cooler run can separate those pairs better while still keeping the last peak near or under 10 min.

At the best tG/T point, changing phi1 may still help if it is moved downward rather than upward, because compressing the useful gradient to the actual elution window could alter the balance between the 3/4 and 6/7 pairs. This is a focused selectivity test around the current optimum while keeping the desirable sub-10 min last peak.

The remaining weakness is a temperature-sensitive early-middle pair, and we have only sampled 35, 40, 45, and 50 C; a larger temperature jump could produce a different selectivity regime rather than the monotonic worsening seen at 50 C. With t_last already safely under 10 min at the best method, this is a high-information probe for a possible order change or separation gain.

60 C changed the pattern substantially, indicating temperature is indeed the main selectivity lever for the critical cluster; 55 C is the missing intermediate that could capture a more favorable compromise before the severe collapses seen at 60 C. This is the best remaining targeted search around the current optimum without sacrificing the zero time penalty.

At 55 C only one pair remains subcritical and the run is comfortably under 10 min, so adding a little gradient time is the cleanest way to improve that pair without incurring any time penalty. This tests whether 55 C with a slightly shallower slope can surpass the current best by pushing the remaining 3/4 pair closer to full credit while keeping t_last below 10 min.

The 55 C series shows the critical 3/4 pair improving as tG increases, and t_last at 14 min is still below 10 min, so one more step to 16 min could increase resolution further while likely keeping the run penalty at zero or very small. This is the most promising remaining way to beat the current best by exploiting the favorable 55 C selectivity with a slightly shallower gradient.

At the best method all peaks likely elute by about phi 0.33, so lowering phi1 to 0.35 should concentrate the entire separation into the active gradient window and may improve the persistent 3/4 selectivity without sacrificing the sub-10 min last peak. This is a different selectivity lever from the temperature and slope scans and is one of the few plausible remaining routes to exceed the current best.

Most geometric changes around the best method have failed, while temperature clearly changes which pair is limiting; 30 C is the only untested cooler setting adjacent to 35 C and may give a different selectivity tradeoff for the persistent 3/4 pair. This is a high-information final temperature probe around the proven best geometry.

At 55 C the only weakness is the 3/4 pair, and raising phi0 tended to improve that pair while 14 min kept t_last under 10 min; combining the favorable 55 C selectivity with a slightly higher phi0 is a plausible remaining route to improve the minimum resolution without a time penalty. The higher phi1 is required by the grid and should have little effect if the late peaks still elute before the gradient end.

At 55 C, 14 min gave a strong but not optimal result, and the disastrous change in injection 23 points to phi0 as the sensitive variable rather than phi1; testing the same successful phi0 with a higher phi1 isolates whether extending the upper window can subtly improve the critical 3/4 pair. This is one of the last untried near-neighbors of the best 55 C condition.

For the final shot, keep the successful fast 55 C regime but shift the whole gradient window slightly lower, which is the one nearby combination not yet tested that could move the persistent 3/4 pair into a more favorable selectivity region while retaining a zero time penalty. It is a targeted last attempt to beat the 12 min, 45 C best by changing window placement rather than slope alone.
